candidates.quote: DJI O3 Enterprise Transmission enables the Mavic 3 Enterprise drones to fly further and transmit signals with higher stability

raw_candidates.quote: DJI O3 Enterprise Transmission enables the Mavic 3 Enterprise drones to fly further and transmit signals with higher stability

attempts.notes: The datalink is DJI's own O3 Enterprise (OcuSync 3) system, so tier 1 is DJI itself; no third-party module vendor exists. The best chip-level evidence comes from the closely related Mavic 3 Pro chip ID (Leadcore IE1000 RF transceiver plus Skyworks front-end modules), which iFixit lists as 'likely' and not for the Enterprise variant specifically — no Mavic 3E-specific teardown naming the RF chipset was found.

verified.evidence_quote: With a maximum control range of 15 km, DJI O3 Enterprise Transmission enables the Mavic 3 Enterprise drones to fly further and transmit signals with higher stability, offering pilots greater peace of mind during flight.
verified.reason: evidence quote does not name the supplier (verifier said low: The page links DJI and the Mavic 3 Enterprise's radio transmission, but it never names SZ DJI Technology Co., Ltd. as the radio supplier or states China.)

raw_candidates.quote: DJI Mavic 3E, DJI Mavic 3T, DJI Mavic 3M by SZ DJI TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD

attempts.notes: The only usable public record I could open was the FCC equipment-authorization filing for the Mavic 3E/3T/3M (FCC ID SS3-M3E2206), which shows the aircraft's radio/datalink is filed by DJI itself; no public teardown identifying the RF silicon inside the O3 Enterprise transmission module was found (iFixit's Mavic 3 Pro chip ID and the TechInsights teardown were paywalled/blocked, and fcc.report PDFs were behind Cloudflare), so no Tier 2 radio-chip candidate could be sourced.
